evidence.quote: As we announced this week, we are purchasing up to $300 billion in Treasury debt, $200 billion of the debt of government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs), and up to $1.25 trillion of mortgage-backed securities guaranteed by the GSEs and federal agencies this year.

Over time, we expect to expand this facility to include loans against other types of newly issued AAA-rated asset-backed securities, such as commercial mortgage-backed securities and private-label residential mortgage-backed securities.
Widening credit spreads, more-restrictive lending standards, and credit market dysfunction are working against the monetary easing and leading to tighter financial conditions overall.
we cannot have a vigorous economic recovery unless we succeed in restoring a reasonable degree of financial stability.
the Committee responded by cutting the target for the federal funds rate to near zero by the end of last year.

parsed.rationale: The speech, largely about community banks and regulatory reform, describes aggressive easing, large-scale asset purchases and planned TALF expansion amid tight financial conditions and a weak outlook. The net signal is dovish, with no discussion of inflation.
